q: The queen's speech had a profound ___ on everyone.
explain: have an impact on. ('affect' is a verb.)

q: After months of practice, her efforts finally paid ___.
The evidence was ___; nobody could argue with it.
We need to ___ the pros and cons before deciding.
He's ___ to win — he's the best by far.
explain: be bound to = be certain to.

q: Swimming is ___ prohibited in the north lake.
The new rules will come into ___ next month.
explain: come into force = start to apply (laws/rules).

q: She ___ out of the competition due to injury.
I can't ___ the difference between the two crystals.
The manager ___ the blame for the mistake.
There has been a sharp ___ in the number of visitors.
explain: a rise (noun) in numbers; 'raise' is mainly a verb.

q: He has a reputation ___ being honest.
Her explanation was ___; I understood instantly.
explain: crystal clear = very easy to understand.

q: We managed to ___ the problem by working together.
explain: overcome a problem = deal with it successfully.

q: He's very ___; he always finishes what he starts.
Which word is the opposite of 'reluctant'?
explain: Reluctant = not wanting to; willing = happy to.

q: Let's try to ___ a compromise.
The new bridge will ___ traffic in the town centre.
Despite the setbacks, the team ___ to finish on time.
Her argument was so ___ that everyone agreed.
We'll need to ___ costs if we want to stay in business.
He's a ___ reader; he finishes a book every two days.
explain: A keen reader enjoys reading a lot.

q: Visits to the tower are ___ appointment only.
explain: by appointment = only if you arrange a time first.

q: The decision was made ___ consultation with local residents.
explain: in consultation with = after discussing with.

q: She was ___ with the job of organising the festival.
explain: be entrusted with = be given responsibility for.

q: His performance ___ all our expectations.
explain: exceed expectations = be better than expected.

q: It's ___ that she'll accept; she seemed very keen.
The company has ___ a new policy on remote working.
explain: adopt a policy = start using it.

q: Which word means 'to make something less serious or painful'?
The two reports are ___ different; you can't compare them.
They ___ a heated argument about money.
explain: get into an argument = start one.
